provider_id_note: A DOCUMENT-IDENTITY KEY, not a provider key inside any engine config. On the opencode substrate provider_id is literally the key of a provider block in the engine's own configuration; this lane runs on the kimi-cli substrate, which has no such block — the engine is the pinned CLI itself, configured through argv, TOML and the KIMI_MODEL_* env channel. The value must still be distinct from every other document's, because loadLaneDocs refuses a duplicate provider id BY NAME and is right to: provider-id resolution takes the first match, so a collision would make one of the two kimi documents silently unreachable.
npm_note: DELIBERATELY EMPTY. The npm field names the ai-sdk provider package opencode loads for a lane (@ai-sdk/anthropic for the kimi lane, @ai-sdk/openai-compatible for zai). This substrate loads none: the engine is the pinned CLI @moonshot-ai/kimi-code@0.38.0, recorded in components.lock as an engine entry rather than here. Declaring @ai-sdk/anthropic to mirror the sibling lane would be a false dated claim in a document whose entire value is that its claims are dated.
endpoint_note: The subscription (Kimi Code membership) endpoint, reached through the CLI's KIMI_MODEL_BASE_URL channel rather than through an engine provider block. Same endpoint as lane kimi and the same vendor warning applies verbatim: "Kimi Code membership benefits and the Kimi Platform have different Base URLs. Please ensure your Base URL and API Key are matched correctly." The SAME HONEST LIMIT also applies: Moonshot does not publish what a membership key does when sent to the metered endpoint (A11 audit U5).
provider_type_note: The KIMI_MODEL_PROVIDER_TYPE value paired with this base URL. It is DATA rather than a Go constant for the same reason the endpoint is: it is a per-lane provider fact with a date, and the engine's own enum is {kimi, anthropic, openai}. The Kimi Code subscription endpoint is documented as OpenAI-protocol at /coding/v1 (the vendor also publishes an Anthropic-protocol base without the /v1 suffix, which this lane does not use). It is set EXPLICITLY rather than left to the engine's default so a default change cannot silently retarget the protocol. VERIFIED 2026-08-26.
pool_note: ONE POOL, TWO LANES. Vendor verbatim, read 2026-08-26 at https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/kimi-code/membership.html: "Kimi Code is the developer-focused AI coding service within Kimi membership benefits, provided together with a Kimi membership subscription and sharing the same quota. Requests from the CLI, VS Code, and third-party tools all count toward that quota." And: "All logged-in devices and API Keys share the same quota". This is the direct primary-source statement that the CLI and api.kimi.com/coding/v1 draw ONE allowance, and it names the CLI explicitly. The consumption side is declared ONCE on the plan document (internal/metering/plandata/kimi.json), which is where a denominator belongs; this row is the lane-side statement of the same fact, and a test pins that both kimi lanes name this identical pool.

recorded_endpoints.note: RECORDED, BUILT ON BY NOTHING. `kimi web` exposes a loopback REST surface carrying a live PLAN-QUOTA READBACK: `{kind:"ok", summary, limits, extra_usage}` where a limits row is `{name?, window:{duration,unit}, used, limit, reset_at?}` with unit one of minute/hour/day/week, plus the pay-as-you-go wallet `{balance_cents, total_cents, monthly_charge_limit_enabled, monthly_charge_limit_cents, monthly_used_cents, currency}`. It CLOSES A11 audit item U3 (the /usage response shape, previously mentioned but never specified) and is the strongest candidate yet for U4 (the missing reset-time signal, which is why reset_marker is empty on both kimi documents). It would be this platform's first provider-signaled OBSERVED overlay outside the Anthropic wire, and it is D4-clean in S10.4's exact sense — an overlay, never the pressure denominator. It is NOT built here and nothing reads it: S10.4's denominator stays the operator's declared budget, and wiring an overlay with no consumer is the class §63 D2 exists to close. A follow-up packet is the place for it (OQ-5).

The international metered Kimi Open Platform endpoint. Recorded so the endpoint self-check owns the wrong-endpoint case by name; never wired. It is ALSO the escape route that does not work: routing around the Gate-A gray zone by swapping to a pay-as-you-go Open Platform key is a DIFFERENT lane — metered, not flat — and G1 P7 keeps the metered-exception list EMPTY at v0 with DeepSeek as the sole pre-registered exception. It would need its own amendment and its own Gate A-C audit, and no Open Platform ToS document was locatable in the 2026-08-26 capture.

credential.note: THE SAME BROKER PROFILE AS LANE kimi, A DIFFERENT VARIABLE NAME — and the difference is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. The vendor states plainly that credential variables "such as KIMI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, and OPENAI_API_KEY are NOT read automatically from shell environment variables", and that "the only exception is the KIMI_MODEL_* family, which is an explicit channel that does read credentials from the shell". So injecting the API lane's KIMI_API_KEY into this CLI authenticates nobody. Two properties of that channel were MEASURED at pin 0.38.0 on 2026-08-26, not assumed: nothing is written back to the config file (the secret never lands on disk), and a missing OR empty key fails with exit 1, the message "provider __kimi_env__ has no credential configured", and ZERO provider calls — fail-closed, never a silent unauthenticated call. One membership means one Console key, so the broker resolves this profile ONCE per spawn and the material fans out to both lanes' variables. No OAuth path is used: `kimi login` and $KIMI_CODE_HOME/credentials/ are not part of this design, and a design that does not need an interactive login should not grow one.

data_policy.statement: The kimi-cli lane carries a no-household-personal-data routing constraint. It is approved for code and general technical work only; household personal data, personal correspondence, and identity-bearing content must never route to it.
data_policy.basis: Identical to lane kimi's, because the constraint is a property of the PROVIDER and not of the client path: operating entity 北京月之暗面科技有限公司 (Beijing Moonshot AI); personal information stored within mainland China; training on inputs is the DEFAULT with only a contact-based opt-out; no GDPR/EEA language. Governing law differs between the two applicable agreements and no page states which binds a membership (A11 audit U6) — the constraint is written to hold under either reading.
data_policy.enforcement_note: RECORDED AND SURFACED, NOT MACHINE-ENFORCED. No per-lane data-policy enforcement point exists in the tree as of 2026-08-26; enforcement lands with the routing-policy seam, and this row is what that seam will read. The rider needs an AFFIRMATIVE operator answer at the gate, not merely an absence of objection.

sanction.note: GATE A IS A RECORDED GRAY ZONE ON BOTH KIMI LANES, not a clean pass, and this row exists so nobody rediscovers that as news. The Community Guidelines state verbatim "Kimi Code subscriptions are for interactive use only" and, as a heading, "Don't use Kimi Code for non-interactive automation" — S03.6 class-3 language, which its own pre-registered watch trigger names and answers with immediate re-audit and lane freeze. The countervailing text is on the same page: it blesses agent frameworks by name ("Kimi CLI, VS Code, Claude Code, OpenCode, OpenClaw"), states that heavy and multi-device use is normal, gives "scripted batch execution or data annotation pipelines" as the banned examples, and describes GRADUATED enforcement ("limiting concurrent access"). The operator ruled PROCEED on 2026-08-26 and the acceptance is recorded in the audit's dated addendum and in S00.9 amendment A12. Two consequences bind the code: the 403 concurrent-request-limit row carries NO documented class (it is also the enforcement signal), and KIMI_CODE_IDENTITY_NAME/_SLUG are never set, because the same page forbids spoofing client identity.

usage_source.note: THE USAGE SOURCE IS THE RUN'S OWN TRANSCRIPT, AND IT CARRIES A RESIDUAL THAT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER. `--output-format stream-json` carries no token or cost field in any frame, so D7 is served by tailing $KIMI_CODE_HOME/sessions/<workDirKey>/<sessionId>/agents/main/wire.jsonl, which records one `usage.record` per model call, live. STRUCTURAL PROTECTIONS IN PLACE: the transcript is pinned by SESSION IDENTITY, never by a glob over sessions/ — on a resume the id is the one `--session` names, and on a start it comes from the engine's own session_index.jsonl filtered to this run's cwd (written when the session is created, before the first model call and therefore before any tool could run). More than one match is REFUSED rather than resolved, and the id the stream finally reports is cross-checked against the one billed from; a mismatch stops billing. RESIDUAL, STATED PLAINLY: the engine requires its data root to be WRITABLE — measured 2026-08-26, a run with the home read-only fails with 'storage write failed: permission denied' even when every subdirectory and every root-level file is pre-created and writable, because it writes atomically (tmp -> rename) and a rename needs a writable DIRECTORY. The engine's own tools share that filesystem namespace. So the compiled config is written 0400 (the engine never rewrites it — a run with all three files read-only exits 0) and the session store is identity-pinned, but a determined tool inside the sandbox can still chmod a config file or write inside the REAL session directory. Total forge-immunity is NOT reachable at this pin. What closes it is the S11.5 injection proxy plus a confinement class that denies the engine home to tool processes; neither is this packet's, and until then this row is the honest statement of what is and is not guaranteed.

default_model_note: K3, matching lane kimi's seat exactly — because the operator's question is which PATH performs better, and a comparison that changed the model as well as the engine would answer neither question. model_routing_note: TIER GATE, NOT REGION GATE — identical to lane kimi, because it is the same membership. region_model_gate stays "none" on every row; the gate is by MEMBERSHIP TIER, is real and enforced on the wire (401 "Your current subscription does not have access to k3"), and the thing that handles it is the model-list-diff canary (P-T17-3). On this lane that canary is the kimi lane's, by name (OQ-4): one Console key means the two lanes cannot be entitled or revoked independently.
overflow_note: overflow_mode is `opt-in-credits` on every model, inherited from the membership rather than from the client path: the Extra Usage Credit Pack is OFF by default, requires funding, and carries an explicitly PROVEN disable (satisfying 3.10 / P-T17-2). Kimi on the web and Kimi Code share the same Extra Usage balance, so this lane and lane kimi also share the spill. RECOMMENDED OPERATOR POSTURE: Extra Usage OFF, under which the lane behaves as a hard stop.

reasoning_effort.note: DELIBERATELY EMPTY AND UNWIRED. The CLI does expose thinking configuration (a [thinking] config section with enabled/effort/keep, observed in the pinned bundle, and the profile.bind frame reports thinkingEffort "on" by default), but no vendor page captured in this packet publishes the accepted effort vocabulary for this engine, and the sibling lane's own value list is already graded unverified-primary from a different source. Declaring a list nobody published would be exactly the false dated claim §64 was written about. No eco_options are declared and no S10.6 rung is invented; the lever stays unwired until somebody captures the vocabulary.

reset_marker_note: DELIBERATELY EMPTY, unchanged from lane kimi and for the unchanged reason (A11 audit U4): no reset-time signal is documented anywhere on the error surface, and the vendor states reset times live in the Console. An empty marker routes depletion to the Class-3 probe park rather than fabricating a Class-2 wait on a time nobody published. The `kimi web` oauth/usage readback recorded above carries a real reset_at and is the candidate that could fill this later — recorded, not wired.
signals_note: DOCUMENTED-NOT-OBSERVED, and pinned EQUAL to lane kimi's table by test. Every row below is a MESSAGE STRING quoted from the vendor's published error reference (https://www.kimi.com/code/docs/en/kimi-code/error-reference.html, first captured 2026-08-24 and RE-READ 2026-08-26, which is where the five newest rows come from), not a body this platform has seen on the wire. The two lanes are held equal deliberately: same membership, same wire, and a divergence would make one lane freeze where the other parks — which the operator, comparing the two lanes, would read as a property of the client path. TRANSPORT NOTE specific to this substrate: the CLI surfaces a terminal provider error ONLY on stderr (measured 2026-08-26 — a provider 403 produced no stdout frame at all), prefixed with its own taxonomy label such as `provider.auth_error:`; retried failures additionally appear on stdout as `turn.step.retrying` meta frames carrying status_code and error_message. The vendor's own caveat applies with extra force here: "If you are using a third-party client such as OpenCode or Claude Code, the client may transform or re-wrap error codes... focus on the text content of the error message". The ceremony's live single-request probe still owes one real 401, one real 429 and, if reachable, one real 403 body before this table is treated as final.

signals.message: You've reached your weekly (7-day) usage limit
signals.note: ADDED 2026-08-26. The 7-day subscription-anchored window emptying is the single most routine failure this lane has; classing it as anything but depletion would page the operator weekly.

ADDED 2026-08-26. A BALANCE event, and it carries NO documented class deliberately: the exemption vocabulary is {transient, depletion, model-drift, endpoint-defect} and has no `balance` member BY DESIGN. So it falls through to the Class-4 status rule and freezes, which is correct — an Extra Usage wallet running dry is not a quota window rolling over, and probe-parking it would wait forever for a top-up nobody is going to make (P-T08-2's failure class).

signals.message: You've reached your concurrent request limit
signals.note: ADDED 2026-08-26, AND IT IS A TRAP — this row carries NO documented class on purpose and the reason must not be optimized away. The string is BOTH an ordinary concurrency shed AND the vendor's stated enforcement action for a terms concern, verbatim from the Community Guidelines: "we'll review the situation first and take appropriate action—such as limiting concurrent access—based on the severity. You'll then see a You've reached your concurrent request limit error." Classing it `transient` would make the platform retry silently THROUGH an enforcement action against the operator's own account — the worst possible response to it, and precisely how a recorded gray zone becomes a terminated subscription. With no class it falls through to the Class-4 status rule (freeze + operator alert), which is the safe half of P-T08-2: recoverable, visible, and it puts a person in front of the decision.
